claim_text: Denmark's ministry says unauthorised people got CPR data on about 11,000 people in a new incident
summary: Denmark's Ministry of Research, Education and Digitalisation said on Nov 26 that the CPR register had found another security incident, in which unauthorised people got access to CPR data on about 11,000 people.
detail: It is the second such incident since October, when the ministry said 8.8 million people's records had been reached.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry press release: "Uvedkommende har skaffet sig adgang til CPR-oplysninger på 11.000 personer" (unauthorised people have gained access to CPR data on 11,000 people); DR and TV 2 report the same from the release.

claim_text: The access came through suspicious lookups in the register from a company, noticed on Monday Nov 23
summary: The ministry says the CPR administration noticed on Monday Nov 23 that there had again been irregular lookups in the CPR system from a company.
detail: Neither the ministry nor the outlets name the company or say whether it is the same one as in October.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: on Nov 23 the CPR administration noticed "igen har været uregelmæssig adfærd i forhold til opslag i CPR-systemet fra en virksomhed"; DR: "Også denne gang har der været tale om mistænkelige opslag i registret fra en virksomhed".

claim_text: The data reached were CPR numbers, names and addresses; people with name and address protection were not included
summary: The ministry says the people involved got lookups of CPR numbers, names, addresses and similar details for about 11,000 people. Names and addresses of people registered with name and address protection were not included.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: access to lookups "vedr. CPR-numre, navne og adresser mv. på cirka 11.000 personer" and it "omfatter ikke navne og adresser på personer, som har valgt at lade sig registrere med navne- og adressebeskyttelse"; DR reports the same.

claim_text: New monitoring of lookups stopped the November incident
summary: The ministry says the incident was stopped by new technical monitoring of lookups, brought in after the October incident. It told DR the monitoring stopped further data from leaking.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: "Hændelsen blev standset af en ny teknisk overvågning af opslag, der blev indført efter den første hændelse"; DR: the ministry told DR the monitoring stopped further leaking of data.

summary: The ministry says the police are investigating both the October and November incidents together with the relevant authorities.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: "Begge sager efterforskes af politiet i samarbejde med relevante myndigheder."

claim_text: A security review of the CPR system is expected to finish before Christmas
summary: The review of the CPR system's security ordered in October is expected to finish before Christmas. Its first conclusions call for modernising the system and tighter rules for companies allowed to look people up.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: the review "forventes afsluttet inden jul" and shows a need for "ændringer af systemet og skærpede krav til de virksomheder, der har adgang til at lave opslag i CPR-registret".

claim_text: In October the ministry said unauthorised people had reached names, addresses and CPR numbers of about 8.8 million people
summary: On Oct 5 the ministry said unauthorised people had misused a Danish company's legitimate access to the CPR system to reach names, addresses and CPR numbers of about 8.8 million registered people, living, emigrated and dead.
detail: Irregular activity during September was noticed on the evening of Oct 2; the company's access was stopped, the Danish Data Protection Agency told, and the police are investigating.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry, Oct 5: "har uvedkommende skaffet sig adgang til navne, adresser, CPR-numre mv. på ca. 8,8 millioner registrerede borgere" by misusing "en dansk virksomheds lovlige adgang"; Help Net Security reports the same figures.

claim_text: The CPR system holds about 11 million registered people
summary: The ministry says the CPR system holds about 11 million registered people, including people who have died or moved abroad, which is why the October figure is larger than Denmark's population.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry, Oct 5: "CPR-systemet rummer i dag ca. 11 millioner registrerede borgere", including the dead and those who moved abroad.

claim_text: Nobody has been named as behind the November incident
summary: The ministry has not said who was behind the November lookups or which company they came from, and the outlets that reported it name no one.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The ministry release and the DR and TV 2 reports name no person, group or company for the November incident.

claim_text: An anonymous person told Politiken that accounts at the company in the October breach used the password 123456; the authorities have not confirmed it
summary: IBTimes UK reports that an anonymous person claiming the October breach told Politiken they got logins through a private company, where at least three accounts used the password 123456. The authorities have not confirmed it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: IBTimes UK: "at least three accounts at the company, including an administrator account, used the password '123456'" and the authorities "have not publicly confirmed the reported password".

claim_text: Danish media traced the October breach to a company on Funen
summary: IBTimes UK reports that Danish media traced the October breach to Pays ApS, a company based on Funen, and that documents obtained by TV 2 showed about 14 million automated searches in ten days.
detail: The ministry has not named the company in its own releases.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: IBTimes UK: "Danish media eventually traced the breach to Funen-based Pays ApS" and "approximately 14 million automated searches in ten days".

claim_text: The ministry says a CPR number is not private and people should prove who they are with MitID
summary: The minister says Danes should get used to the CPR number not being private and prove who they are with MitID. The ministry says never give out a password, even to someone who knows your name, address and CPR number.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Ministry: "vi skal vænne os til, at CPR-nummeret ikke er privat, og at vi i stedet skal benytte bl.a. MitID til at bevise, hvem vi er", and never hand out passwords "selvom modtageren tilsyneladende kender dit navn, adresse og CPR-nummer".

claim_text: Online discussion of the October breach turned on the 123456 password report and on whether CPR numbers should be treated as secret
summary: In Hacker News threads on the October breach, many commenters took up the 123456 report and argued a CPR number is not a secret. The threads are where these questions are raised, not proof of anything.
detail: No thread about the November incident was found.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The two Hacker News threads (229 and 348 comments) carry these points from many separate commenters.

claim_text: The CPR administration supplies personal data to public authorities and private companies
summary: The CPR administration is part of the ministry's department and, through the Central Person Register, is the central supplier of personal data to public authorities and the private sector.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CPR office about page: the administration sits in the ministry's department and works as "central leverandør af personoplysninger til offentlige myndigheder og til den private sektor".
